description.en: Eastern and central Galilee: Tiberias and 'Arraba tax farms, Nazareth, and north-east Galilee (Ba'na); Tiberias held against attacks from Damascus 1738-1743.

sources.quote: The governor of Sidon himself appointed Zāhir as the tax farmer of both Tiberias and ՙArraba, a town located farther west, near Acre.
Ẓāhir al-ʿUmar (c. 1737–75) dominated the political life of northern Palestine for nearly 40 years.

description.en: Galilee with Acre (seized 1746) as capital, influence extended to Haifa and Tantura; Jaffa held briefly in the early 1770s.

sources.quote: In 1746, he took the city by force, killed the local multazim, and took his place.
Zāhir was successful in keeping Damascus at bay and expanding his influence to Haifa and Tantura.
He then took advantage of retreating Egyptian forces and conquered the coastal city of Jaffa.
Zahir al-'Umar, the powerful magnate of Palestine from 1746 to 1775, was the first to develop Akka into a major port at the expense of Saida.
